title: It’s normal to feel lonely
text: Everyone feels lonely in their first year.It’s a normal part of moving to a new city. Your first friends might be nomads just like you. Many will leave, and it might hurt.It gets easier with time.You will meet people who choose to stay, just like you. Berliners are not the friendliest strangers. It’s normal to miss small talk and nice interactions. It gets better when you learn German, but you also get used to it. It just takes time. Everyone feels lonely at first, but it gets better. You will slowly rebuild your social circle, discover new passions, meet new people. It just takes time and a bit of effort.

section: How to meet people in Berlin
title: Meetups
text: Meetup.comThere are meetup groups for all kinds of hobbies, and just for meeting people. Many meetups are in English. Eventbrite Facebook events InterNationsThey organise free events for immigrants. TimeleftHave dinner with strangers. Board gamesThere are a fewboard game meetups. English speakers are welcome. It’s easier to meet people around a shared hobby like chess or bouldering. Meeting strangers is always a little awkward, but it’s easier if you have something to do at the same time.

section: How to meet people in Berlin
title: Apps
text: Bumble BFFA dating app, but for making friends. /r/berlinsocialclubA subreddit for making friends in Berlin. English speakers are welcome.

section: How to meet people in Berlin
title: Communities
text: If you are a student, go to orientation week, and join your school’s Erasmus community. They organise many activities for international students. There are groups and organisations for every nationality in Berlin. Here are a few: Americans in Berlin Brazilians in Berlin Canadians in Berlin Dutch in Berlin French speakers in Berlin Indians in Berlin Koreans in Berlin Nigerians in Berlin Poles in Berlin Russians in Berlin Turks in Berlin

section: How to meet people in Berlin
title: Other ways to make friends
text: Take German lessonsLearning Germanis important, and it’s also a good way to meet people. You cantake a class, orjoin a language tandem. VolunteerUseVostelto find where to volunteer. You can help even if you don’t speak German.
